findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate docs/exit-codes.md:177 as a consumer to update: document how `--changed-since` reconciles with the current 'missing id -> 2' contract (e.g. selection mode exits 0 with no criterion id).
evidence: docs/exit-codes.md:177: `criteria eval <id>` runs calibration fixtures live; empty or missing id → 2; unknown criterion → 1
Current parser (_parsers/advanced/llm_eval.py:39-43) makes `criterion_id` a REQUIRED positional; _criteria_eval returns 2 when it is blank
AC#2/#5 require a `--changed-since` invocation with NO criterion id to exit 0 and issue no model call — i.e. 'missing id' must now succeed, not return 2
findings.finding: The `criteria` command's exit-code contract in docs/exit-codes.md ('empty or missing id -> 2') is a consumer outside the CLI code dir that the new `--changed-since` mode contradicts and the plan does not enumerate for update.
scenarios: A `--changed-since` invocation supplies no positional criterion id; the documented 'missing id -> 2' rule would either be violated or, if enforced, block the new mode
findings.suggested_fix: Add docs/exit-codes.md to the edit set and state that `criteria eval --changed-since <ref>` makes the positional `criterion_id` optional, exiting 0 for the selection mode while preserving 'missing id AND no --changed-since -> 2'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the changed-rubric mapping recognizes BOTH the packaged `reviewers/plan_review_<id>.md` and the project-override `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-<id>.md` conventions, and add an AC covering the override-path case (or explicitly scope the job to packaged rubrics and justify why override edits are out of scope).
evidence: Packaged rubrics confirmed at src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T8.md, plan_review_G6.md (underscore prefix)
criteria/ids.py: PLAN_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX = 'plan-review-' and create_prompt writes .rebar/prompts/<id>.md, so a project override rubric is .rebar/prompts/plan-review-<id>.md (dash prefix)
prompts.get_prompt resolves a project .rebar/prompts/<id>.md override that WINS over the packaged reviewers/*.md copy — so an override edit is a genuine rubric change
findings.finding: The changed-file->criterion-id mapping is specified for only one of the two rubric storage conventions. A criterion's rubric can live at the packaged path `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<id>.md` (underscore prefix) OR at a project override `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-<id>.md` (dash prefix, from `criterion_prompt_id`). The plan's ACs exercise only the packaged `plan_review_<id>.md` form; the Approach never states whether an edit to a `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-*.md` override is also mapped, so a project rubric regression may be silently missed.
findings.location: Approach ('a shared engine function maps a changed-file set to the criterion ids whose rubric files appear in it') and Acceptance Criteria 1/3
scenarios: A project ships or edits `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-T8.md` overriding the T8 rubric; the changed-file set contains only that dash-prefixed path and the selector maps nothing, so the regression escapes the very trigger this epic exists for.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the new selection function inverts/reuses the existing fixture_selection.rubric_path resolution (and note the code_review glob-trigger machinery as prior art) rather than reimplementing the criterion<->rubric-file mapping, so the two surfaces cannot drift.
evidence: fixture_selection.py:71 rubric_path(criterion_id, *, repo_root, gate_key='plan_review') already resolves criterion -> rubric file via effective_routing/criterion_prompt_id and get_prompt override-wins ordering
code_review/registry.py:340 glob_triggered_overlays(changed_files, ...) and :373 project_criterion_applies(criterion_id, changed_files, ...) already map changed files to criterion ids
The plan text does not cite either as prior art nor say the new function builds on rubric_path
findings.finding: The plan's proposed 'shared engine function [that] maps a changed-file set to the criterion ids whose rubric files appear in it, resolving each against effective_routing(...) and its prompt id' duplicates an existing engine primitive: rebar.llm.evals.fixture_selection.rubric_path(criterion_id, *, repo_root, gate_key) already resolves a criterion id to its rubric file via criterion_prompt_id + get_prompt override-wins ordering against the packaged reviewer prompt, and the code_review registry already maps changed_files to criterion ids via glob_triggered_overlays / project_criterion_applies / select_project_applicability. The plan does not name this prior art or state whether the new function reuses rubric_path for the per-criterion resolution or reimplements it, risking a second, drifting copy of the rubric-path rule.
findings.location: Approach — 'a shared engine function maps a changed-file set to the criterion ids whose rubric files appear in it'
scenarios: A rubric override at .rebar/prompts/<pid>.md changes the resolved path; if the new function reimplements resolution it may diverge from rubric_path's override-wins ordering and select the wrong (or no) criterion

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how `--changed-since` coexists with the existing required positional `criterion_id` on `rebar criteria eval` (optional positional + mutual exclusivity, or a distinct subcommand), so the invocation parses.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/llm_eval.py:40-43 — `p_eval.add_argument("criterion_id", ...)` is a required positional on the existing `eval` subparser
src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:119-121 — empty/missing criterion id returns exit 2
docs/exit-codes.md:177 — 'criteria eval <id> runs calibration fixtures live; empty or missing id -> 2'
findings.finding: The plan proposes `rebar criteria eval --changed-since <ref>` as if adding a flag to the existing `eval` verb, but that verb already takes a REQUIRED positional `criterion_id` and errors (exit 2) when it is empty/missing; the plan never states whether the positional becomes optional, is made mutually exclusive with `--changed-since`, or whether a new subcommand is introduced. As written, the proposed invocation would fail argparse before any selection runs.
findings.location: Approach ('The CLI exposes it as `rebar criteria eval --changed-since <ref>`')
scenarios: A developer runs `rebar criteria eval --changed-since origin/main` and argparse rejects it for the missing positional criterion_id
The workflow job invokes the command with no criterion id and the job fails at parse time
findings.suggested_fix: Make `criterion_id` optional and mutually exclusive with `--changed-since` (argparse mutually-exclusive group), or introduce a distinct subcommand (e.g. `rebar criteria eval-changed --changed-since <ref>`); state the chosen grammar in the Approach.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion (or documented rationale) verifying the workflow job supplies the correct --changed-since ref per trigger (PR base vs push before-sha), not merely that the workflow is actionlint-valid.
evidence: Scope names 'the workflow job that calls it' as a deliverable
Testing covers 'A unit test covers the workflow's resolved spec list' and 'existing actionlint test node covers workflow validity' but not the command invocation / ref derivation
No AC asserts the --changed-since value the job supplies per trigger
findings.finding: The workflow job is a named deliverable, but no acceptance criterion verifies that the job actually invokes the command with a correctly-derived changed range for its trigger events; the ACs cover the CLI selection function and actionlint validity, but the job's command wiring (which git ref it passes as --changed-since for a pull_request vs an ordinary push) is uncovered.
scenarios: The job runs but passes the wrong ref (e.g. empty or full-history), selecting everything or nothing, and actionlint + spec-list tests still pass

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether `--changed-since` selection reuses the live `calibrate_criterion` path per selected criterion (and how the empty-selection 'no model call, exit 0' case short-circuits before any credential/model requirement), reconciling it with the existing single-criterion live-run semantics.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:98-102 — the existing verb executes a criterion's fixtures LIVE and 'Needs the agents extra + credentials'
src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:154-155 — calls calibrate_criterion for the single criterion
Plan AC: 'A range touching no rubric file selects nothing, exits 0, and issues no model call ... with no model configured'
findings.finding: The existing `rebar criteria eval <id>` runs exactly ONE criterion LIVE through its Pass-1 finder (calibrate_criterion), requiring the `agents` extra + credentials. The plan's new mode selects MULTIPLE criteria and, per AC, a non-rubric range 'issues no model call' and runs 'with no model configured'. The plan does not reconcile this select-and-run (possibly no-model) behavior with the existing verb's single-criterion always-live semantics.
findings.location: Approach + Acceptance Criteria (non-rubric range 'issues no model call ... with no model configured')
scenarios: A non-rubric range runs the command in a CI/dev environment with no credentials and must exit 0 without a model call, but the existing verb path assumes a live calibration run
A rubric-touching range needs to run the selected criteria's fixtures — the plan does not say whether selection reuses the live calibrate_criterion path per selected id

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the git ref the workflow job passes to --changed-since for each included trigger (e.g. PR: base ref; push: before-sha), so the CI wiring is unambiguous.
evidence: 'a developer runs the command locally against any git range'
the workflow's per-event ref (PR base branch vs push before-sha) is not stated

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the shared function inverts a changed `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_*.md` path to criterion id(s): reconcile the underscore-vs-hyphen filename/prompt-id difference and the forward-only/non-reversible `criterion_prompt_id` map (ids.py), and state how a multi-criterion rubric file (e.g. `plan_review_G1G2.md`) selects all its ids.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:26-29 states the map is 'deliberately one-way: ... the sanitized id is NOT reversibly split back to the dotted id — the dotted id is always carried explicitly, never reverse-derived.'

On-disk rubric files live at src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<id>.md with UNDERSCORES (e.g. plan_review_T8.md, plan_review_G6.md), whereas criterion_prompt_id(id) yields 'plan-review-<id>' with HYPHENS (ids.py:49-62) — the changed git path is the reviewers file, not the prompt id.

src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ contains plan_review_G1G2.md — a single rubric file whose criterion id is 'G1G2' (one entry), and plan_review_no-file-impact.md / plan_review_ac_process_gate.md / plan_review_hedge.md use prompt-name spellings, so a bare filename->criterion-id map is not a plain criterion_prompt_id application.
findings.finding: The plan's mechanism ('maps a changed-file set to the criterion ids whose rubric files appear in it, resolving each against effective_routing and its prompt id') rests on reversing the criterion-id->prompt-id mapping, but that mapping is documented as forward-only and non-reversible, the on-disk rubric filenames differ from the prompt id, and some files bundle multiple criteria.
findings.location: Approach section, sentence: 'a shared engine function maps a changed-file set to the criterion ids whose rubric files appear in it, resolving each against criteria.effective_routing(...) and its prompt id'
scenarios: Implementer wires the function using only criterion_prompt_id(effective_routing keys) and cannot invert a changed reviewers/*.md path to a criterion id.
A rubric edit to plan_review_G1G2.md must select both G1 and G2 but the described forward-resolution logic yields a single id 'G1G2'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the resolution DIRECTION as forward-enumeration — build the {rubric-path -> criterion-id} set from `effective_routing` ids (each id -> its packaged and override rubric filename) and intersect with the changed-file set — because `criteria/ids.py` documents the id->prompt-id map as forward-only / non-reversible.
evidence: criteria/ids.py docstring: 'It is deliberately one-way: a name may contain dashes, so the sanitized id is NOT reversibly split back to the dotted id — the dotted id is always carried explicitly, never reverse-derived.'
criterion_prompt_id does `criterion_id.replace('.', '-')`, an unambiguous forward map only
findings.finding: The plan describes resolution as reverse-parsing each changed rubric path to a criterion id ('resolving each against criteria.effective_routing'), but the id->rubric-id map is documented as FORWARD-ONLY and non-reversible: a project criterion name may contain dashes, so `plan-review-project-foo-bar.md` cannot be uniquely split back to a criterion id. A structurally-more-robust direction is to enumerate the registry ids forward (via effective_routing) to each id's rubric filename(s) and test the changed-file set for membership.
findings.location: Approach ('resolving each against criteria.effective_routing(".", gate_key="plan_review") and its prompt id')
scenarios: A project criterion `project.foo-bar` whose rubric is `plan-review-project-foo-bar.md` is edited; a path->id reverse parser cannot recover `project.foo-bar` because the dashes are ambiguous, so it either warns spuriously (AC3-style) or mis-maps.
